passage: onevent() and finish() invoke the reporters in construction order, so every reporter sees events and the finish signal in the same order. tick() reaches only the reporters that opt into ticking.
dummy ancestors put the fragment at document depth without indenting text nodes; their lines are stripped below.

each testcase is rendered to its xml fragment as its event arrives; live testresult objects (which may carry large captured-output payloads) are never retained, only the rendered strings and bounded per-class counters.

tags are stable and additive only; the schema is documented in docs/architecture/jsonl.md.
the caller owns the resource lifecycle; this class never opens or closes the stream.

onevent() writes one line per finished test as it arrives. finish() prints failure and error details after the run, then a final summary including worker recycling counts and the skipped tests with their reasons.
high utilisation is the healthy state, so the bands run green at 90%, yellow at 70%, and red below, making idle workers stand out.
pad outside the colour codes so escape sequences cannot break the alignment.

per worker: busy time is the sum of its class spans, the window runs from its spawn (or first class, whichever is known) to its last class finish, and utilisation is busy over window. boot latency is spawn to first class start, which includes the hello handshake and first assignment wait.
class events use worker clocks; worker and run events use orchestrator clocks. all are host wall clocks, so cross-process boot latency may include scheduling delay.

only tests over the threshold are reported, so fast suites get no extra noise. the default footer caps at five lines; extended mode (--profile) keeps twenty-five.
duration colours escalate at one and five seconds.

every message carries a flowid set to the class name, keeping interleaved parallel output untangled for consumers. the class name identifies the flow because a class never spans workers and, unlike a worker id, it is present on test events as well as class events.
dim name and count read as pending; the failure mark and the duration keep their colours so failures and slow classes stay visible.
a permanent line has to land now, so it rides its frame past the throttle; a clean pass just waits for the next scheduled repaint.

in bounded mode a cleanly passing class prints nothing permanent; only classes containing failures or skips append a line, the moment they finish. --verbose restores a permanent line per class. without cursor support, every class is appended instead.
the first permanent line opens the scrollback block with a blank line so it never butts against the header; later lines stack directly under it.
the window's own leading blank line provides the gap in cursor mode; append-only output needs it written here.
